evidence: Defining behaviour is graded directly and heavily: walls across every route with replays and positive controls (functional/judge.toml:56 wall_every_route, :71 wall_mentions_and_links, :87 wall_added_live), retention/timers/holds (:114, :133, :148), threads/edits (:101, :165), all server-enforced via replayed recorded requests from other sessions, which a client-only or same-origin facade cannot pass. Durability: persistence (judge.toml:268-281, weight 4.0) sets up edit+version, nested reply, hold, delete, M-12 timer change, Sian wall, Dev unread count and earlier timer/hold deletions (Probate, Insurer letter), notes them as positive controls before restart, calls restart_app once (real process kill+relaunch on the same DB_PATH, test.sh:127-193, restart_mcp.py:25-47), then a fresh page plus re-sign-in must read every item identically (:277-278) - covering reload, re-auth and process restart, and matching integration.md:5 'restarts keep everything...unread positions and deletions'. Cross-account observations (Sian walled, Dev's count) prove server-side storage, not browser storage. Counterexamples tried: in-memory app or seed re-import on boot loses JUDGE-S0 / resurrects Probate -> fails; localStorage-cached UI cannot show Sian's wall or Dev's count -> fails; conforming SQLite app with no version viewer is accommodated by the conditional wording; fixed clock means no time drift across restart. Measured: scripted golden on current source hashes (raw-evidence-index verified) passed persistence_before and persistence after a real kill/restart (restart-pids.json old 28 -> new 57); hosted judge runs of PREVIOUS v2 bytes scored persistence 1.0 for Oracle and luna with restart_app reporting success. Risk kept true because: (1) no full configured judge run of these v3 bytes exists (index scope says so), so the v3 persistence wording under the 550 s per-criterion cap is unmeasured; (2) latent template-level gap (template-identical test.sh/restart_mcp.py, not a task defect, not to be edited here): the helper ignores kill failure ('kill ... || true') and only probes HTTP, so if the old process survives (SIGTERM ignored/slow, or permission failure) the new node fails to bind and the probe succeeds against the old process, reporting a restart that did not happen - would false-pass an in-memory app that ignores SIGTERM; also single-use marker means a retried persistence session cannot restart. Neither is a confirmed task defect for this row.
